rules: Only effect sizes stated in a paper (abstract or full text) appear in reported_effect; anything else is 'not reported'.
No value here was estimated, interpolated or converted from a figure.
Where a paper reports only a direction, the proposed parameter change carries a free magnitude to be fitted against the published phenotype, not a number invented here.

Operators are limited to: remove neurons; remove synapses/connections; scale presynaptic release strength; shift excitability (threshold or spike-frequency-adaptation strength); scale active-zone strength; short-term-depression parameters.

reported_effect.stated_change: -46% in threshold current; -57% in threshold charge transfer (5132.8 +/- 1091.32 -> 2197.4 +/- 484.46 pA*ms)
supporting: Kv4 current density -37% in mushroom body neurons (same DOI)
IA reduced in MB neurons but not projection neurons: 10.1016/j.neuroscience.2017.06.008
reported_effect.unchanged_controls: capacitance 1.9 +/- 0.1 -> 1.8 +/- 0.1 pF; resting potential -52.8 +/- 2.3 -> -49.1 +/- 1.7 mV; input resistance 2.5 +/- 0.1 -> 2.4 +/- 0.2 GOhm (all not significant)

proposed_parameter_change.statement: -46% threshold current (equivalently -57% threshold charge) -> downward shift of firing threshold, magnitude to be fitted so that rheobase falls by 46% in the model's LIF units

reported_effect.measure: synaptic vesicle release probability; Ca2+-channel cluster density; Bruchpilot amount; bouton number
reported_effect.stated_change: age-dependent reduction in release probability, in Ca2+-channel cluster density and in Brp, with increased pre/postsynaptic contact length and NO bouton loss
supporting: 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.3699-09.2010 (same model: reduced vesicle pools, faster synaptic fatigue, 39 +/- 12% successful central responses)
10.1016/j.celrep.2018.06.029 (independent group: late-stage presynaptic depression in adult projection neurons, +70% inter-event time)

proposed_parameter_change.statement: -Y% release probability -> presynaptic scale (1 - Y) with Y fitted; the only published anchor for Y in an adult central neuron is the +70% inter-event time (i.e. release rate x0.58) from 10.1016/j.celrep.2018.06.029
hold_fixed: synapse count (no bouton loss was reported)
proposed_parameter_change.fit_target: not reported in the source paper; use the 0.58 release-rate ratio from the companion adult dataset as the initial guess

candidates.age_staging: progressive; detectable at the ages at which the model's locomotor phenotype appears (14-21 days)

reported_effect.measure: T-bar size (EM); BRP ring diameter (STED); BRP/RBP gold particles per T-bar; odour-evoked SynaptopHluorin signal; active zones per bouton area

proposed_parameter_change.statement: +X% active-zone strength and +X% release probability on ALPN->KC* with a compensating reduction in synapse count per connection; X to be fitted so that the simulated odour-evoked release rises while the postsynaptic KC response does not (the published signature)
proposed_parameter_change.fit_target: qualitative triple constraint: presynaptic release up, AZ number per bouton down, postsynaptic response flat-to-slightly-down
proposed_parameter_change.note: because release goes up while AZ number goes down, a single scalar increase in synaptic weight is NOT a faithful implementation

reported_effect.measure: PN hyperpolarisation and firing suppression evoked by optogenetic activation of GABAergic local interneurons; LN self-inhibition; PN odour tuning

reported_effect.case: dfmr1-: markedly reduced hyperpolarisation and significantly weaker firing suppression (n=16); LNs show sustained depolarisation and firing (n=16, p=6.5e-4); PN lifetime sparseness reduced (p=9.8e-14)

proposed_parameter_change.operator: scale_presynaptic_release (and optionally remove_synapses) on ALLN outputs

reported_effect.measure: synaptic fatigue rate (inverse decay constant of EJC amplitude during 100 Hz, 250 pulses); presynaptic mitochondria and vesicle pools; central response success rate
reported_effect.control: 100% successful responses with direct motor axon stimulation
reported_effect.case: 39 +/- 12% successful responses on brain stimulation (p<0.01); fatigue rate increased with age, earliest and strongest for Abeta-Arctic
reported_effect.stated_change: -61 percentage points in central response success rate; fatigue rate increase not reported numerically; vesicle pools reduced and vesicle size increased by 21 days; no change in terminal size

proposed_parameter_change.statement: set short-term depression so that sustained 100 Hz transmission fails progressively, with a central transmission success rate of 0.39 as the published anchor; fatigue is use-dependent (no effect at 10 Hz), so the change must be in depression dynamics, not in baseline weight alone
proposed_parameter_change.fit_target: success rate 0.39 +/- 0.12 at high frequency, with near-normal transmission at 10 Hz

candidates.condition: Abeta42 (and, as contrast arms, tau and alpha-synuclein) in photoreceptors

reported_effect.measure: percentage of ommatidia with a full complement of 7 intact rhabdomeres; ERG depolarisation amplitude
reported_effect.control: 92% of ommatidia intact at 30 days (97% at 10 days)
reported_effect.case: Abeta42: 56% at 30 days (p<0.001); tau: 92% at 30 days (no loss) but progressive ERG loss; alpha-synuclein: 89% at 10 days (p<0.001) and not countable at 30 days
reported_effect.stated_change: Abeta42 photoreceptor survival 0.61 of control at 30 days; tau 1.00 of control with ERG failure; alpha-synuclein 0.92 of control at 10 days
reported_effect.sample: ~100 ommatidia per 100x field, >=4 animals per genotype per timepoint

proposed_parameter_change.statement: Abeta42: delete 39% of R1-R6 (56/92 survival). alpha-synuclein: delete 8% of R1-R6 at the 10-day equivalent (89/97). tau: keep all cells and scale R1-R6 presynaptic release down until the simulated visual response falls, since the ERG falls while cell number is preserved
proposed_parameter_change.fit_target: Abeta42 cell survival 0.61; alpha-synuclein 0.92; tau survival 1.00 with reduced transmission

candidates.note: the only shortlisted state in a cell type the model's existing visual memory tasks drive directly, so it is the natural first implementation and the natural C5 test

excluded_candidates_and_reason.C06_tau_panneuronal_reversible: fails C2 and C3: mechanism is protein-synthesis-dependent memory (translation/plasticity), no representable parameter measured
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C08_aging_dpm_to_ab_kc_connectivity_loss: fails C3: DPM is annotated dopaminergic in this model, so its synapses carry zero weight and removing DPM->KC contacts is functionally silent
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C09_dopamine_neuron_dysfunction_pd: fails C3: dopaminergic synapses carry zero weight; the measured mechanism is neuromodulation
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C10_fragilex_5ht2a_loss: fails C3: serotonin receptor signalling; serotonergic synapses carry zero weight and there is no receptor operator
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C19_sleep_loss_plus_abeta_arctic_hyperex: fails C3 in effect: l-LNv is annotated serotonergic, so an imposed excitability change cannot propagate
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C20_asyn_sleep_loss_d1_dependent_memory_: fails C2 and C3: dopamine receptor transcripts only; sleep history is not a model variable
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C21_aging_kc_fibre_number_decline: fails C1: single 1984 study, fibre profiles rather than cell counts, contradicted by modern aging work that finds synaptic rather than cellular change
excluded_candidates_and_reason.C24_tau_dopaminergic_release_loss: fails C3: dopaminergic release, zero weight in this model
